title: Theft of Blueprints
statementMd:
Insurgents accidentally got hold of the plan of a top secret research polygon created on a distant planet for the needs of the Galaxy Empire. The insurgents suppose that this polygon is developing new deadly weapon. The polygon consists of $*n*$ missile silos connected by bidirectional underground passages. The passages are linked to laboratories where research is conducted. Naturally, the passages are guarded severely: the passage between silos $*i*$ and $*j*$ is patrolled by $*c*_{*i*, *j*}$ war droids.

The insurgents studied the polygon plan and noticed its unusual structure. As it turned out, for any $*k*$-element set of silos $*S*$ there is exactly one silo that is directly connected by a passage with each silo from $*S*$ (we'll call this silo adjacent with $*S*$). Having considered that, the insurgents decided to act as follows:

1. they choose a $*k*$-element set of silos $*S*$;
2. a group of scouts lands from the air into each silo from $*S*$;
3. each group moves along the corresponding passage to the silo, adjacent with $*S*$ (as the scouts move, they check out the laboratories and watch for any signs of weapon blueprints);
4. in the silo, adjacent with $*S*$, the groups get on the ship and fly away.

The danger of the operation is the total number of droids that patrol the passages through which the scouts will go. The danger of the operation obviously only depends on the way to choose set $*S*$. The insurgents haven't yet decided on the exact silos to send the scouts to. However, they already want to start preparing the weapons for the scout groups. To do that, the insurgents need to know the mathematical average of the dangers of the operations that correspond to all possible ways to choose set $*S*$. Solve this problem to help the insurgents protect the ideals of the Republic!

## Input

The first line contains two integers $*n*$ and $*k*$ ($2 ≤ *n* ≤ 2000$, $1 ≤ *k* ≤ *n* - 1$) — the number of silos and the number of scout groups, correspondingly. The next $*n* - 1$ lines describe the polygon plan: the $*i*$-th of these lines contains $*n* - *i*$ integers $*c*_{*i*, *i* + 1}, *c*_{*i*, *i* + 2}, ..., *c*_{*i*, *n*}$ — the number of droids that patrol the corresponding passages (-$1 ≤ *c*_{*i*, *j*} ≤ 10^{9}$; if $*c*_{*i*, *j*} =$ -$1$, then silos $*i*$ and $*j*$ don't have a passage between them). All passages are bidirectional, that is, we can assume that $*c*_{*i*, *j*} = *c*_{*j*, *i*}$. No passages connect a silo with itself. It is guaranteed that the polygon plan meets the conditions of the problem statement.

## Output

Print the average danger of the scouting operation, **rounded down to an integer**. Note that at the given limits the answer to the problem **always** fits into the standard integer 64-bit data type.

Please do not use the `%lld` specifier to write 64-bit integers in С++. It is preferred to use the `cout` stream or the `%I64d` specifier.

## Note

In the first sample there are 6 one-element sets of silos. For sets ${1}$, ${5}$ the operation danger will equal 8, for sets ${3}$, ${6}$ — 3, for sets ${2}$, ${4}$ — 5. The mathematical average equals ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/3bc833659595c25e73150ed7f23907011961ceca.png).

In the second sample there are 3 two-elements sets of silos: ${1, 3}$ (danger equals 21), ${1, 2}$ (danger equals 11), ${2, 3}$ (danger equals 10). The average operation danger equals ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/02946ba8c525c97041629189ab4acc976074d8d1.png).

## 题目描述

叛乱分子意外获得了银河帝国为自身需要在一颗遥远行星上建造的顶级秘密科研基地的设计图。叛乱分子猜测，这个基地正在研发一种新型致命武器。基地由 $*n*$ 个导弹发射井组成，这些发射井之间由双向地下通道连接。通道通往进行研究的实验室。自然，通道受到严密守卫：发射井 $*i*$ 和 $*j*$ 之间的通道由 $*c*_{*i*, *j*}$ 个战斗机器人巡逻。

叛乱分子研究了基地的设计图，并注意到了它非同寻常的结构。事实证明，对于任意一个包含 $*k*$ 个发射井的集合 $*S*$，都恰好存在一个发射井，它通过通道与 $*S*$ 中的每一个发射井直接相连（我们称这个发射井与 $*S*$ 相邻）。考虑到这一点，叛乱分子决定采取如下行动：

1. 选择一个包含 $*k*$ 个发射井的集合 $*S*$；
2. 一组侦察兵从空中降落到 $*S*$ 中的每个发射井；
3. 每组侦察兵沿对应的通道前往与 $*S*$ 相邻的发射井（在移动过程中，他们检查实验室并留意武器蓝图的任何迹象）；
4. 在与 $*S*$ 相邻的发射井中，各组侦察兵登上飞船并离开。

此次行动的危险程度，是侦察兵将经过的通道上巡逻的战斗机器人的总数。显然，行动的危险程度只取决于集合 $*S*$ 的选择方式。叛乱分子还没有决定具体派侦察兵前往哪些发射井。然而，他们已经想开始为侦察小组准备武器。为此，叛乱分子需要知道对应于所有选择集合 $*S*$ 的行动危险程度的数学平均值。请解决这个问题，帮助叛乱分子捍卫共和国的理想！

## 输入格式

第一行包含两个整数 $*n*$ 和 $*k*$（$2 ≤ *n* ≤ 2000$，$1 ≤ *k* ≤ *n* - 1$）——发射井的数量以及侦察小组的数量。接下来的 $*n* - 1$ 行描述基地的设计图：其中第 $*i*$ 行包含 $*n* - *i*$ 个整数 $*c*_{*i*, *i* + 1}, *c*_{*i*, *i* + 2}, ..., *c*_{*i*, *n*}$——巡逻相应通道的战斗机器人的数量（$- $1 ≤ *c*_{*i*, *j*} ≤ 10^{9}$；如果 $*c*_{*i*, *j*} =$ -$1$，则发射井 $*i*$ 与 $*j*$ 之间没有通道）。所有通道都是双向的，也就是说，可以认为 $*c*_{*i*, *j*} = *c*_{*j*, *i*}$。发射井与自身之间没有通道。保证基地的设计图满足题目描述中的条件。

## 输出格式

输出侦察行动危险程度的平均值，**向下取整**为整数。注意，在给定限制下，答案**始终**可以用标准的 64 位整数类型表示。

请不要在 C++ 中使用 `%lld` 格式说明符来输出 64 位整数。建议使用 `cout` 流或 `%I64d` 格式说明符。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，共有 6 个包含一个发射井的集合。对于集合 ${1}$、${5}$，行动危险程度为 8；对于集合 ${3}$、${6}$，行动危险程度为 3；对于集合 ${2}$、${4}$，行动危险程度为 5。数学平均值等于 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/3bc833659595c25e73150ed7f23907011961ceca.png)。

在第二个样例中，共有 3 个包含两个发射井的集合：${1, 3}$（危险程度为 21）、${1, 2}$（危险程度为 11）、${2, 3}$（危险程度为 10）。行动危险程度的平均值等于 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/02946ba8c525c97041629189ab4acc976074d8d1.png)。
